title.narrative: UNICEF contributed to setting child poverty at the center of the public agenda through evidence-based analysis, advocacy and policy dialogue highlighting progress made and persistent inequalities and challenges. Technical assistance to subnational governments contributed to developing tools to measure the cost of raising children -including disability considerations- and improving access to child-support. UNICEF also advanced studies on food insecurity and non-monetary poverty. Partnerships with grassroots organizations enhanced outreach to vulnerable populations, in particular in rural areas. Efforts to support children with disabilities included municipal action plans, access to certification, and research on care, contributing to more inclusive social protection systems.
Policies and programmes are influenced by analysis and advocacy to reduce child poverty, Text
